old_caption: The video captures a close-up view of several crayons arranged vertically on a white surface. The crayons are of various colors, including orange, yellow, green, black, blue, pink, and red. Some of the crayons have been used, as evidenced by the melted wax at their tips, which has dripped down onto the surface below. A black object, possibly a cup or container, is positioned above the crayons and remains stationary throughout the video. The background remains consistently white throughout the video, emphasizing the vibrant colors of the crayons and the contrast created by the melted wax. There are no animals or characters present in the scene, and the focus remains solely on the crayons and the black object above them. The camera maintains a steady position, providing a clear and detailed view of the objects.

caption: The video captures a white vertical surface holding twelve crayons standing tip-down in three loose clusters. A left group of red-brown, yellow, green and black sits beside a middle group of orange, yellow, dark blue and orange Crayola, with a right group of pink, yellow Crayola, peach and black. Colored drag streaks in red, yellow, green and black mark the surface beneath the left cluster, and orange and yellow trails run under the middle cluster. The crayons and these streaks remain fixed in position relative to the frame throughout the segment, showing no translation, rotation or deformation. A dark cup-shaped object intrudes from the top-left corner, partly out of frame at the start. Over the course of the clip this object drifts gradually rightward and downward. It increases its extent within the frame and shifts its position against the white background. The view stays continuous with no cut, and this slow movement is the only visible change while the arranged crayons hold their places.

not ground truth. Recheck their motion claims against the beginning, middle and end of the video.

Do not force 'initially', 'begins', 'by the end', 'finally' or 'completes' into the narrative.
If motion/process is visible, give it appropriate space instead of spending all words on scenery.
Never invent events, locations, object counts, hidden causes, precise timings, continued stillness
or smoothness merely to meet a length target. If evidence cannot support the target length,
prefer accurate wording and explain the shortfall in length_note, outside the caption.
Finish every sentence. Avoid redundant atmospheric padding and unsupported 'likely' guesses.
